bib.title: How Can We Know What Language Models Know?

question: How can we tighten the lower bound on factual knowledge in LMs by finding better prompts than hand-written ones?
hypothesis: Manually written prompts are sub-optimal, so any single prompt gives only a lower bound on what the LM knows; mined, paraphrased and ensembled prompts should retrieve more.
contributions: Top-K rank ensemble and optimized weighted ensemble of prompts
Analysis of prompt consistency, POS patterns and cross-model transfer
Release of LPAQA, the LM Prompt And Query Archive

method.summary: Generate many cloze prompts per relation by mining Wikipedia (middle-word and dependency-path) or back-translation paraphrase, rank them on a held-out train set, and average log-probabilities of the top K or learn softmax prompt weights. BERT, ERNIE and KnowBert themselves are frozen; only per-relation prompt weights are learned.
method.task: Factual knowledge probing by cloze-style relation completion (LAMA)

datasets.name: LAMA T-REx
datasets.size: at most 1000 subject-object pairs per relation, 41 relations; avg 830.2 pairs, 767.8 unique subjects, 150.9 unique objects, object entropy 3.6

datasets.name: T-REx-train
datasets.size: avg 948.7 pairs per relation, 354.6 unique objects
datasets.preprocessing: single-token objects only; used to mine prompts, rank prompts, learn weights

datasets.name: Wikipedia
datasets.source: sentences containing subject and object, distant supervision, for prompt mining
datasets.preprocessing: drop prompts that are only stopwords/punctuation or longer than 10 words

other.use: back-translation paraphrasing, B=7 candidates each way

training.objective: maximize probability of gold objects P(y|x,r) under softmax-weighted log-linear prompt ensemble (Eq. 3); LM frozen

other.trainable_parameters: T times number of relations (T=40, 41 relations)

inference.decoding: argmax over vocabulary of masked-slot probability, single token
inference.samples: one deterministic pass; no seeds reported
inference.prompting: cloze template with x and y slots, y masked

parameters.T: 40 most frequent prompts from mining or paraphrasing
parameters.B: 7 back-translation candidates, B^2 ranked by round-trip probability
parameters.K: top K prompts averaged, K in 1..10, Top1/3/5 reported
parameters.dedupe: drop prompts of stopwords only or over 10 words

metrics.name: micro-averaged accuracy
metrics.definition: per-relation fraction of pairs where argmax prediction equals the single ground truth, averaged over relations (LAMA P@1)

metrics.name: macro-averaged accuracy
metrics.definition: per-relation accuracy computed for each unique object then averaged

metrics.name: prediction divergence
metrics.definition: fraction of pairs where two prompts differ in success

eval.protocol: Single run per setting, no seeds or significance tests reported; ensemble weights learned on T-REx-train and tested on T-REx.
